items.title: Ella Langley Beats Out Taylor Swift for Single of the Year at 2026 CMAs
items.summary:
Taylor Swift ’s return to the 2026 CMA Awards was all the talk in Music City — but in a surprising twist, she didn’t take home any trophies.

Ella Langley beat out Swift, 36, on Wednesday, November 18, for Single of the Year , the first award handed out during the celebratory evening.

Swift was nominated for “I Knew It, I Knew You” from Toy Story 5 , while Langley, 27, won for “Choosin’ Texas,” produced by the singer herself, as well as Miranda Lambert and Ben West .

Langley, who was nominated in the same category for her song, “Be Her,” also bested powerhouse singers Lainey Wilson , who hosted the awards show, and Cody Johnson .

2026 CMA Awards Arrivals: Stars Deliver Country Couture on the Red Carpet 

“I love this song,” Langley said during her acceptance speech. “We just sat in a room and did our best one afternoon and it is the gift that just keeps on giving.” (Langley walked the red carpet solo after Us previously confirmed that she is dating country singer Tucker Wetmore .)

She gushed, “I’m just grateful to be a part of it. I truly am. I can’t believe this is my life and what’s going on is absolutely insane. I just can’t believe it’s me this is happening to.”

Ella Langley and Miranda Lambert. Cindy Ord/Getty Images 
 Swift, for her part, has never won a CMA in the category but she was previously nominated in the award in 2013 for “Highway Don’t Care,” recorded with Tim McGraw and Keith Urban .

Bristowe, who was the lead for season 11 of The Bachelorette in 2015, assured fans that she would not be applying for the new season.

“Do I have a boyfriend? I do,” she said on a panel hosted by Jared Freid . “It feels a little more intentional, a little more honest. I don’t feel like I have a stage mom as a partner.”

items.title: Wife, Daughter Arrested 4 Years After Man's Severed Head Was Found: Sheriff
items.summary:
A California man’s wife and daughter have been arrested in his murder more than four years after the discovery of his severed head inside a trash bag, authorities said.

The breakthrough comes after cold case investigators eventually identified the male victim as Paul Wesley Fitzmaurice Jr. , who lived in Citrus Heights with his wife and daughter, according to the Placer County Sheriff’s Office.

Authorities were initially unable to identify him due to decomposition after his severed head was found in the Todd Valley area of Foresthill on September 28, 2024, authorities said.

An investigation revealed Fitzmaurice’s daughter, Mary Fitzmaurice , allegedly killed him inside their home and then worked with her mother, Fitzmaurice’s wife Georgia “Gwenn” Fitzmaurice , to get rid of his body, the Placer County Sheriff’s Office said in a Wednesday, November 18, news release.

Couple Hid Lover's Body Under Air Mattress, Stole His Social Security Benefits 

Mary, 45, was taken into custody on murder charges while Georgia, 75, was arrested on accessory charges, according to the agency.

Paul had never been reported missing, authorities said. Mary and Georgia are accused of maintaining to friends and family that he was alive while they allegedly collected his Social Security checks and pension, per The Sacramento Bee .

Placer County District Attorney Morgan Gire said at a Wednesday news conference that the office plans to file murder charges against Mary in connection with Paul’s death, according to the newspaper.

Thoughts and half-price prayers with Poundland, please. The discount chain has been on the verge of collapse for a while, and its future looks bleak. Now, to add to the ignominy, David Beckham is kicking it while it’s down.

Not literally, by the way: I suppose I should spell that out since we’re dealing with a litigious billionaire. I did not mean to imply or cause a reasonable person to infer that Sir David is standing on Brixton high street kicking a Poundland. Rather, DB Ventures, the licensor of the David Beckham brand, is causing a bit of a stink about the fact that the football legend’s fragrance range was found on sale in the discount store as well as at other purveyors of budget goods. It is now suing the perfume company, Coty, which it further accuses of under reporting sales, for $41m (£31m).
